newsitem.title: USA: Two companies cut workers due to UPS strike.
newsitem.headline: Two companies cut workers due to UPS strike.

text.p: Two companies said they laid off 200 workers because of the United Parcel Service strike -- Russ Berrie and Co. Inc., a maker of plush dolls and gift items, and National TechTeam Inc., a provider of data services.
Russ Berrie, based in Oakland, N.J., said Wednesday it cut 100 part-time and temporary employees because the strike has reduced its ability to ship goods.

"At this time of year, we're shipping a lot of seasonal and Christmas items. We can't find enough sources to get out the products," President Curts Cooke said. "We're getting out about 20 to 30 percent of our normal shipments."
If the UPS strike ends, the employees laid off Friday probably would be rehired, Cooke said. The size of the company's work force was not immediately available.

National TechTeam, based in Dearborn, Mich., said it has temporarily laid off about 100 employees who worked with a 175-member team that provides technical support to customers tied to United Parcel Service's computer system.
National TechTeam, which employs 1,500 workers, plans to offer the workers temporary jobs on other projects until the UPS strike ends.
"We want to be sure we can retain all of these people," National TechTeam Chief Executive Officer William Coyro said by telephone.
The strike by 185,000 Teamsters at UPS entered its 10th day Wednesday with no talks scheduled between the union and the nation's largest package delivery company.
UPS normally handles 12 million packages a day, 80 percent of them shipped by ground nationwide, and many businesses have struggled to deliver goods or find alternate shippers.
UPS Chairman James Kelly said Tuesday that 15,000 Teamsters could lose their jobs if the strike lasted two weeks. Union officials dismissed the statement as a threat.
